operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are mixed-case with underscores (Ref_Document_Types, Date_in_Locaton_To); must be double-quoted verbatim in generated SQL.
Typo in schema: 'Date_in_Locaton_To' (missing 'i') — must be preserved exactly, not corrected.
DATETIME columns store text like '1972-03-31 09:47:22' (space-separated, no T, no timezone); ts_fuzzer dispatches to Date|Number(int elements) — first element is not int so Date path.

Ref_Calendar.Calendar_Date is a DATETIME PK and is the FK parent for 6 child date columns (Date_Stored, Date_in_Location_From, Date_in_Locaton_To, Planned_Destruction_Date, Actual_Destruction_Date) — date values must be drawn from parent's generated set, not fresh.
Document_Locations has composite PK (Document_ID, Location_Code, Date_in_Location_From) — composite-PK members get max_l0=30 cap.
Documents_to_be_Destroyed has two FKs to Employees (Destruction_Authorised_by_Employee_ID, Destroyed_by_Employee_ID) — same parent, two child columns.
All_Documents.Document_ID is parent of both Document_Locations.Document_ID and Documents_to_be_Destroyed.Document_ID (1:1-ish child PKs).
Document_Description, Other_Details (All_Documents, Employees, Documents_to_be_Destroyed) are 100% NULL, distinct=0 — String sampler gets empty element list, p:=1, all fresh random strings.
Gender_MFU CHAR(1) has samples ['', '1'] — storage text, distinct=2, values are empty string and '1' (not 'M'/'F'/'U').
Ref_Document_Types.Document_Type_Description and Ref_Locations.Location_Description are all empty string (distinct=1) — String sampler with single '' element.
Ref_Locations.Location_Code values are single lowercase letters ('b','c','e','n','x') — CHAR(15) but 1-char values.
All tables are tiny (4–15 rows); no huge-table sampling needed, but read_schema must still handle rowid ORDER BY.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer on DATETIME columns: template inferred from first parsable element = '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'; range = [min,max] of parsed originals (e.g. 1972..2017); fresh dates uniform in that range.
Ref_Calendar.Calendar_Date is a single-column PK -> max_l0=inf, so fresh dates never reused; child FK date columns draw from parent's final filtered set with replacement.

String fuzzer on CHAR/VARCHAR: length range from originals (e.g. [0,20] default for empty columns, [1,15] for codes); 50% contaminate adds/drops chars — likely produces implausible codes like 'BKx' or 'B'.
Number fuzzer on INTEGER PKs (Document_ID, Employee_ID): range [-10^4,10^4] (scale=4 default), perturbed by ±1/±2 — likely produces negative or huge IDs, driving FN on range predicates.
Number fuzzer on Day_Number (INTEGER, distinct 7, values 1–8): list range [min(el), 10^4] due to upstream quirk (list_max overwritten by full max) — fresh draws can be huge.
Gender_MFU CHAR(1) with elements ['','1']: String sampler length range [0,1], 50% contaminate may produce 2-char strings violating CHAR(1) affinity (sqlite accepts, no error).
Empty-string-only columns (Document_Type_Description, Location_Description): String sampler with one '' element, p=1 -> all fresh random strings, no empty strings — likely FP on '= ''' predicates.
100% NULL columns: String sampler with no elements -> p:=1, all fresh random strings (never NULL) — likely FP on IS NULL predicates.
FK consistency: child FK columns draw from parent's FINAL filtered values; if parent PK dedup drops rows, child may reference missing parent (FK pragma OFF, no error) — likely FP on join predicates.
Composite PK (Document_Locations): sample_fresh_primary_keys drops duplicate tuples; Date_in_Location_From drawn from Ref_Calendar (15 values) so collisions likely, many rows dropped.
Documents_to_be_Destroyed.Document_ID FK to All_Documents: 1:1 child PK, drawn from parent's 15 IDs; dedup keeps first occurrence — small table.
No CHECK constraints, no UNIQUE indexes beyond PKs — drop_unique_duplicates only acts on PKs; NOT NULL violations (e.g. Gender_MFU='') pass sqlite affinity.
